title: Secundum quid: complete in its own kind
source_text: III. Secundum quid perfectum est illud cui nihil deest, non simpliciter, sed in suo genere, id est, quod habet omnem perfectionem naturae suae congruam & debitam. Ita perfectus equus est cui nihil deest quod pertinet ad naturam equinam, & perfecta planta quae habet omnem perfectionem plantae convenientem, quamvis absolute loquendo, sint multae perfectiones quas non habet equus, vel planta quae perfecta dicitur.
pass_a_gloss: Secundum quid perfect is that to which nothing is lacking, not simply, but in its own genus, that is, which has every perfection congruent and due to its nature. So a perfect horse is one to which nothing is lacking that pertains to equine nature, and a perfect plant which has every perfection suitable to a plant, although absolutely speaking there are many perfections which a horse, or a plant called perfect, does not have.
pass_b_english: Secundum quid: nothing lacking in its own kind.
Perfect horse / perfect plant = full for that nature.
